title.ja: Nitro: EC2 を支えるしくみ、Nitro Enclaves、Graviton
title.en: Nitro: What EC2 Stands On, Nitro Enclaves, and Graviton

sources.title: Instances built on the AWS Nitro System
supports: The Nitro System's components are Nitro cards (local NVMe storage, networking, management, monitoring, security), the Nitro security chip on the motherboard, and the Nitro hypervisor, which manages memory and CPU allocation
Instances built on the Nitro System use ENA for enhanced networking and see storage volumes as NVMe block devices
Lists which virtualized and bare metal families are built on each Nitro version (v2 to v6); T4g, M6g, C6g and T3 are Nitro v2
A bare metal instance can take 20 minutes or more from the running state until it is reachable
AWS Graviton processors only support Linux operating systems and need an arm64 AMI

sources.title: AWS Nitro System
supports: AWS's statement that the Nitro System delivers practically all of the compute and memory resources of the host hardware to instances

sources.title: The Security Design of the AWS Nitro System: introduction
supports: The whitepaper was published on November 18, 2022 and last updated on February 15, 2024
The Nitro System is the underlying platform for all EC2 instances launched since the beginning of 2018
Its three key components are the Nitro Cards, the Nitro Security Chip, and the Nitro Hypervisor

sources.title: Traditional virtualization primer
supports: A classical virtualization host needs device models and a general-purpose operating system beside the VMM; in early EC2 this was an Amazon Linux VM running as Xen's dom0

sources.title: The Nitro System journey
supports: Starting with C5 in 2017 the Nitro System eliminated dom0; a minimized hypervisor based on KVM provides the VMM, and what device models did moved to Nitro Cards

sources.title: The components of the Nitro System
supports: Nitro Cards provide all I/O interfaces and all outward-facing control interfaces, on hardware physically separate from the system main board that runs customer workloads
Nitro Cards present NVMe for block storage and ENA for networking over PCIe, divided into SR-IOV virtual functions assigned directly to VMs
Encryption keys for EBS, instance storage and VPC networking are present in plaintext only in the protected volatile memory of the Nitro Cards
The Nitro Controller is the hardware root of trust and the only gateway between the server and the EC2 control plane
The Nitro Security Chip mediates writes to firmware and holds the main board in reset until the controller has verified it, which is what makes bare metal instances possible
The Nitro Hypervisor has no networking stack, no general-purpose file system, no peripheral device drivers, no shell and no interactive access mode

sources.title: Putting the pieces together: EBS volume attachment
supports: Attaching a volume ends with the Nitro Card for EBS presenting an NVMe device and the hypervisor sending a hot-plug event to the VM
The volume's data key is decrypted in KMS, re-encrypted to the host's public key, and kept in plaintext only in the volatile memory of that Nitro Card

sources.title: No AWS operator access
supports: AWS's statement that there is no mechanism for any system or person to log in to EC2 Nitro hosts, access the memory of EC2 instances, or access customer data on encrypted instance storage or encrypted EBS volumes
Operators can use only a limited set of authenticated, authorized, logged and audited administrative APIs, none of which gives access to customer data
The stated trade-off: some issues cannot be debugged in place and must be reproduced on dedicated non-production hardware

sources.title: The EC2 approach to preventing side-channels
supports: Fixed performance instances get dedicated cores and memory; CPU cores are never shared simultaneously between customers through SMT
Burstable instances (T3, T3a, T4g) can use overcommitted CPU and memory and can run one after another on the same core, with state flushed between them
Graviton instances get multiples of one vCPU because the hardware has no SMT; SMT hardware gives multiples of two
A Nitro Enclave inherits the same isolation and side-channel mitigations as any EC2 instance; its vCPUs (at least one full core) and memory are hot-unplugged from the parent

sources.title: The Security Design of the AWS Nitro System: conclusion
supports: Since the beginning of 2018, all new EC2 instance types are based on the Nitro System

sources.title: AWS Nitro System gets independent affirmation of its confidential compute capabilities
supports: AWS engaged NCC Group for an architecture review of the Nitro System; AWS's post of 2023-05-09 quotes the report: "As a matter of design, NCC Group found no gaps in the Nitro System that would compromise [AWS] security claims"
The claims the post says were validated, including that no administrative API can access customer content on the host
sources.note: An AWS blog post about a report AWS commissioned. The report itself was not read for this chapter.

sources.title: Amazon EC2 instance type naming conventions
supports: A name is series, generation, options, then the size after a period, or metal for bare metal
The series letters and the option letters copied into examples/68-nitro/src/instance-type.ts (a, g, i for the processor; b, d, e, flex, n, q, z for capabilities)
The page lists neither a series Gr or DL nor an option f, and does not state the order of option letters

sources.title: Specifications for Amazon EC2 general purpose instances
supports: m6g.large: 8 GiB, AWS Graviton2, 2 vCPUs, 2 cores, 1 thread per core; m7g is Graviton3, m8g Graviton4, m9g Graviton5
m6i.xlarge: 4 vCPUs on 2 cores, 2 threads per core
The security table marks Nitro Enclaves as supported for m6g.large and not for t4g.micro or t3.micro

sources.title: Specifications for Amazon EC2 compute optimized instances
supports: c6g.large: 4 GiB, AWS Graviton2, 2 vCPUs, 2 cores, 1 thread per core; c7g is Graviton3, c8g Graviton4, c9g Graviton5
c6i.xlarge: 8 GiB, 4 vCPUs on 2 cores

sources.title: Amazon EBS volumes and NVMe
supports: EBS volumes are exposed as NVMe block devices on Nitro instances; the names in a block device mapping are renamed to /dev/nvme[0-26]n1, possibly in another order

sources.title: Map Amazon EBS volumes to NVMe device names
supports: Device nodes are created in the order devices respond, so an NVMe device name can change between instance starts
The EBS volume ID is the NVMe serial number (shown without the hyphen); `lsblk -o +SERIAL` lists it
Amazon Linux provides a udev rule that creates a symbolic link from the block device mapping name (for example /dev/sdf) to the NVMe device, and the ebsnvme-id command
AWS recommends stable identifiers: the volume ID, or the file system's UUID or label

sources.title: Device names for volumes on Amazon EC2 instances
supports: The device name given at attach time is used by EC2; the block device driver may assign another name
Amazon Linux creates a symbolic link for the name you specified; other operating systems could behave differently

sources.title: Amazon EBS-optimized instance types
supports: t3.micro, t4g.micro, c6g.large and m6g.large are in the list that is EBS-optimized by default, with no way and no need to turn it on
The types where it must be enabled for an hourly fee are previous generations (c1, c3, i2, m1, m2, m3, r3)

sources.title: Enable enhanced networking with ENA on your EC2 instances
supports: Enhanced networking on Nitro instances goes through the Elastic Network Adapter and needs an AMI with the ENA driver

supports: The options --json, --nodeps and --output used in examples/68-nitro/src/volume.ts

sources.title: AWS Graviton Processors
supports: AWS's statement that Graviton-based instances cost up to 20% less than comparable x86-based instances
t4g instances are powered by Graviton2; Graviton5 exists as of 2026-10-13

sources.title: Selecting and configuring an instruction set architecture for your Lambda function
supports: Lambda's arm64 architecture runs on AWS Graviton2
Before moving a function to arm64: every third-party dependency, layer and extension needs an arm64 version, and a container image has to be rebuilt for the architecture

sources.title: Amazon ECS task definitions for 64-bit ARM workloads
supports: 64-bit ARM tasks run on Graviton with Fargate (Linux only, platform version 1.4.0 or later); the page does not name a Graviton generation

sources.title: What is Nitro Enclaves?
supports: An enclave is a separate, hardened virtual machine with only a local socket to its parent instance: no persistent storage, no interactive access, no external networking
Data and applications inside the enclave cannot be accessed by processes, applications, or users (root or admin) of the parent instance
The list of parent instance types: no T family, no x86 .large (M6i, C6i start at xlarge), Graviton families from .large (M6g, C6g except medium and metal)
Up to four enclaves per parent; enclaves stop when the parent stops; hibernation and enclaves cannot be enabled together; supported in all Regions
There are no additional charges for Nitro Enclaves beyond the instance and other services used

sources.title: AWS Nitro Enclaves FAQs
supports: Nitro Enclaves is not available on bare metal instances, burstable instance types (for example T3), and instances with only one CPU core

sources.title: Nitro Enclaves concepts
supports: An enclave is a VM with its own kernel, memory and CPUs, made by partitioning memory and vCPUs from the parent instance
The KMS proxy runs on the parent; sessions with KMS are established logically between KMS and the enclave, and the traffic is protected from the parent
The vsock is the only channel an enclave has; the parent's CID is always 3

sources.title: Enclave workflow overview
supports: The three parties (data owner, parent instance administrator, application developer); the parent instance administrator should have no permission to use the key or to change the key policy
The decryption flow: the enclave sends the encrypted data key with its attestation document through the parent's KMS proxy, and KMS encrypts the plaintext key to the enclave's public key

sources.title: Cryptographic attestation
supports: The six measurements: PCR0 (image file), PCR1 (kernel and bootstrap), PCR2 (application), PCR3 (parent's IAM role), PCR4 (parent's instance ID), PCR8 (signing certificate)
PCR0 to PCR2 are printed by nitro-cli build-enclave; PCR3 and PCR4 are SHA-384 over 48 zero bytes followed by the ARN or the instance ID, with the example values the tests check
Enclaves started with --debug-mode or --attach-console produce attestation documents whose PCRs are all zeros, unusable for attestation
An attestation document can be requested only from inside the enclave

sources.title: Using cryptographic attestation with AWS KMS
supports: The example key policy: Allow for the instance role on kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:GenerateRandom with StringEqualsIgnoreCase on kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384 and PCR keys
If the request does not include an attestation document, the role has no permission because the condition cannot be satisfied

sources.title: Verifying the root of trust
supports: The attestation document is CBOR, signed as COSE_Sign1 with ECDSA 384, with the fields module_id, timestamp, digest, pcrs, certificate, cabundle and the optional public_key, user_data, nonce
Documents are signed by the AWS Nitro Attestation PKI, whose root certificate is published with its fingerprint

sources.title: Nitro Enclaves security
supports: Enclaves use the same Nitro Hypervisor isolation that separates EC2 instances to isolate their vCPUs and memory from the parent

sources.title: Building an enclave image file
supports: An enclave image file is made from a Docker image with nitro-cli build-enclave, which prints the measurements

sources.title: Creating an enclave
supports: A parent instance is launched with --enclave-options 'Enabled=true'
Image files can be built with the Nitro CLI on any Linux environment, also outside AWS; running an enclave needs a parent instance

sources.title: Getting started: Hello Enclaves sample application
supports: The commands of the walkthrough: docker build of /usr/share/nitro_enclaves/examples/hello, nitro-cli build-enclave, run-enclave, describe-enclaves, console, terminate-enclave
The tutorial is written for an m5.xlarge and preallocates 2 vCPUs and 512 MiB

sources.title: Getting started: Connect the parent instance with an enclave by using virtio-vsock
supports: A vsock address is a 32-bit CID and a 32-bit port; the first enclave gets CID 16 by default and the parent is CID 3
The guide's example passes the role's temporary credentials from IMDSv2 into the enclave over vsock, in Python, with the parent application in a container
Virtio-vsock libraries are available for languages such as Rust, Go and Python

sources.title: Getting started: Connect an enclave with AWS KMS
supports: The image file contains unencrypted copies of all code and data, so secrets must not be part of it
vsock-proxy on the parent listens on CID 3 port 8000 and forwards to the KMS endpoints in /etc/nitro_enclaves/vsock-proxy.yaml; TLS runs between KMS and the enclave
kmstool-enclave-cli creates an ephemeral key pair, requests an attestation document from the NSM device with the public key, and attaches it to the Decrypt request
A debug enclave's PCR0 is 96 zeros; otherwise PCR0 is read from nitro-cli describe-enclaves

sources.title: Install the Nitro Enclaves CLI on Linux
supports: On Amazon Linux 2023: dnf install aws-nitro-enclaves-cli and aws-nitro-enclaves-cli-devel, the ne and docker groups, the allocator service, the docker service
The allocator preallocates 512 MiB and 2 vCPUs by default (/etc/nitro_enclaves/allocator.yaml); on a Graviton instance with 2 vCPUs it must preallocate only 1

sources.title: nitro-cli run-enclave
supports: The options --cpu-count, --memory (at least 64 MiB), --eif-path, --enclave-cid (4 and higher), --debug-mode
With multithreading the parent keeps at least 2 vCPUs and the enclave takes an even number; without it the parent keeps at least 1

sources.title: nitro-cli build-enclave
supports: The options --docker-uri, --docker-dir, --output-file, --private-key and --signing-certificate; a signed image also gets PCR8

sources.title: nitro-cli terminate-enclave
supports: The options --enclave-id, --enclave-name and --all

sources.title: kmstool-enclave-cli
supports: The decrypt and genkey commands and their parameters; output is PLAINTEXT: and CIPHERTEXT: followed by base64
It is meant to be called as a subprocess from any language, with libnsm.so beside it
sources.note: Read on the main branch on 2026-10-13. Not built and not run.

sources.title: aws-nitro-enclaves-cli: allocator.yaml
supports: The file has two settings, memory_mib: 512 and cpu_count: 2, and an optional cpu_pool

sources.title: Cryptographic attestation support in AWS KMS
supports: With a signed attestation document, Decrypt, DeriveSharedSecret, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyPair and GenerateRandom return the plaintext encrypted under the public key from the document instead of the plaintext
GenerateDataKey still returns the copy of the data key encrypted by the KMS key

sources.title: AWS KMS condition keys for attested platforms
supports: The default key policy allows the account every action including Decrypt; AWS recommends least privilege and mentions NotAction kms:Decrypt as one way to restrict it

sources.title: Condition keys for Nitro Enclaves
supports: kms:RecipientAttestation:ImageSha384 corresponds to PCR0, and kms:RecipientAttestation:PCR<PCR_ID> to a named PCR; both are single-valued strings for key policies and IAM policies
Both are effective only when the Recipient parameter carries a signed attestation document; without one, permission is denied because the condition is not satisfied
StringEqualsIgnoreCase is the operator AWS's examples use for PCR values

sources.title: How to make attested calls to AWS KMS
supports: The Recipient parameter carries the document and the key encryption algorithm; the response has CiphertextForRecipient and an empty Plaintext
KMS relies on the document's signature; you cannot supply your own certificate to sign it
AWS SDKs take the Recipient parameter; the document comes from the Nitro Secure Module through the NSM API

sources.title: Monitoring attested requests
supports: CloudTrail entries for attested requests carry a recipient field in additionalEventData

sources.title: KMS API: Decrypt
supports: Recipient and CiphertextForRecipient as request and response fields; Plaintext is null or empty when CiphertextForRecipient is present

sources.title: KMS API: RecipientInfo
supports: AttestationDocument (up to 262144 bytes) and KeyEncryptionAlgorithm, whose only valid value is RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256

sources.title: Default key policy
supports: A KMS key policy gives no permission to the account or its identities unless a statement says so
A statement whose principal is the account lets IAM policies allow the listed actions; without it IAM policies that allow access are ineffective

sources.title: KMS key access and permissions
supports: The key policy alone can control access when the key and the IAM principal are in the same account

sources.title: AWS::EC2::Instance
supports: EnclaveOptions has one member, Enabled, and updating it requires replacement
Hibernation and Nitro Enclaves cannot be enabled on the same instance

sources.title: How Instance Metadata Service Version 2 works
supports: The PUT response hop limit is 1 by default; a bigger one may be needed for container services running on the instance

definition.ja: いまの EC2 のインスタンスが載っている土台。ネットワークとストレージの入出力を専用のカード（Nitro Card）に移し、ホストの CPU には CPU とメモリを分けるだけのハイパーバイザーを残した構成。Nuxt のサーバーエンジンの Nitro とは別物。
definition.en: What today's EC2 instances stand on: network and storage I/O moved to dedicated cards (Nitro Cards), and a hypervisor on the host CPU that only divides CPU and memory. Unrelated to the Nitro server engine of Nuxt.

definition.ja: Nitro System のハイパーバイザー。CPU とメモリをインスタンスに割り当て、Nitro Card のデバイスを渡すだけで、ネットワークスタックもシェルも持たない、と AWS は説明している。
definition.en: The hypervisor of the Nitro System. AWS describes it as allocating CPU and memory and handing Nitro Card devices to instances, with no network stack and no shell.

definition.ja: AWS が設計した Arm（arm64）のプロセッサー。インスタンスタイプの名前では g の文字で表される。
definition.en: The Arm (arm64) processors AWS designs. In an instance type name, the letter g.

definition.ja: インスタンスの vCPU とメモリの一部を切り出して作る、隔離された仮想マシン。ネットワークも永続的なストレージも対話的な入口も持たず、親インスタンスとは vsock だけでつながる。
definition.en: An isolated virtual machine carved out of an instance's vCPUs and memory. It has no network, no persistent storage and no interactive access, and reaches its parent instance over vsock only.

definition.ja: エンクレーブに vCPU とメモリを渡し、エンクレーブを起動して止める EC2 のインスタンス。
definition.en: The EC2 instance that gives an enclave its vCPUs and memory, and starts and stops it.

glossary.ja: エンクレーブイメージファイル

definition.ja: エンクレーブで起動する OS とアプリを 1 つにまとめたファイル（.eif）。Docker のイメージから nitro-cli build-enclave で作る。
definition.en: The one file (.eif) with the operating system and application an enclave boots. Built from a Docker image with nitro-cli build-enclave.

definition.ja: platform configuration register。エンクレーブのイメージや親インスタンスの素性から計算した SHA-384 のハッシュ。PCR0 はイメージファイル全体の計測値。
definition.en: Platform configuration register: a SHA-384 hash computed from the enclave's image or from facts about its parent. PCR0 measures the whole image file.

glossary.ja: アテステーションドキュメント

definition.ja: Nitro Hypervisor が署名する文書。エンクレーブの PCR と、エンクレーブが渡した公開鍵が入っている。エンクレーブはこれを見せて、自分がどのイメージから起動したかを外に証明する。
definition.en: A document signed by the Nitro Hypervisor, carrying an enclave's PCRs and a public key the enclave supplied. The enclave shows it to prove which image it was started from.

definition.ja: 仮想マシンとそのホストの間のソケット。アドレスは CID とポートの組で、エンクレーブと親インスタンスをつなぐ唯一の経路。
definition.en: A socket between a virtual machine and its host, addressed by a CID and a port. The only path between an enclave and its parent instance.

summary.ja: 68章のスタックを AWS に一度もデプロイしていない。cdkd 0.296.28 の EC2 のプロバイダーは `EnclaveOptions` を扱わず、指定があるとインスタンスを Cloud Control API 経由に回す、とインストールした版のコードにある。その経路でエンクレーブ対応のインスタンスが作れること、Principal だけで権限を与えるキーポリシーを KMS が受け付けること、明示した管理用のアクションだけで cdkd がキーを作って消せることが未確認。
summary.en: The chapter 68 stack has never been deployed. The installed cdkd 0.296.28 does not wire `EnclaveOptions` in its EC2 provider and routes an instance that sets it through Cloud Control API. Unverified: that this route creates an enclave-enabled instance, that KMS accepts the key policy, and that the listed administrative actions are enough for cdkd to create and delete the key.

resume.ja: 11章をデプロイした後に `vp run nitro:infra:deploy`。`aws ec2 describe-instances --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].EnclaveOptions'` が `Enabled: true` を返すことを見て、`vp run nitro:infra:drift` を通す。終わったら `vp run nitro:infra:destroy`（インスタンスは時間課金）。
resume.en: After deploying chapter 11, run `vp run nitro:infra:deploy`, check that `aws ec2 describe-instances --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].EnclaveOptions'` returns `Enabled: true`, and run `vp run nitro:infra:drift`. Then `vp run nitro:infra:destroy` (the instance is billed by the hour).

summary.ja: エンクレーブを一度も起動していない。Graviton の 2 vCPU のインスタンスで allocator を 1 vCPU にして hello のサンプルが動くこと、`--cpu-count 1` で起動できること、既定のルートボリュームに Docker のイメージとイメージファイルが収まること、hop limit 1 のままユーザーガイドの親側のコンテナが IMDSv2 から認証情報を取れるかどうかが未確認。
summary.en: No enclave was ever started. Unverified: that the hello sample runs on a 2-vCPU Graviton instance with the allocator set to 1 vCPU and `--cpu-count 1`, that the default root volume holds the Docker images and the image file, and whether the user guide's parent container can read credentials from IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1.

resume.ja: デプロイの後、Session Manager で入り、本文「エンクレーブを起動するまで」の順に `dnf install`、allocator の設定、`docker build`、`nitro-cli build-enclave`、`run-enclave --debug-mode`、`console`、`terminate-enclave` を通す。
resume.en: After the deploy, enter with Session Manager and follow the page's steps in order: `dnf install`, the allocator setting, `docker build`, `nitro-cli build-enclave`, `run-enclave --debug-mode`, `console`, `terminate-enclave`.

summary.ja: KMS のアテステーションを一度も通していない。この章のキーポリシーで、エンクレーブの中からの Decrypt と GenerateDataKey が通り、親からの同じ呼び出しが拒否されることは、ドキュメントの記述と自作の評価器でしか確かめていない。ノートを封印する TypeScript のコード（`src/enclave/vault.ts`）をエンクレーブのイメージにする部分（vsock の待ち受け、NSM からのドキュメントの取得、`kmstool_enclave_cli` の呼び出し）は、このリポジトリに無い。
summary.en: KMS attestation was never exercised. That Decrypt and GenerateDataKey succeed from inside the enclave and are refused from the parent under this chapter's key policy is known only from the documentation and from the book's own evaluator. The part that would turn the TypeScript vault (`src/enclave/vault.ts`) into an enclave image (a vsock listener, the attestation document from the NSM, the call to `kmstool_enclave_cli`) is not in this repository.

resume.ja: ユーザーガイドの「Connect the parent instance with an enclave by using virtio-vsock」と「Connect an enclave with AWS KMS」をそのまま通す。`nitro-cli build-enclave` が出した PCR0 を `vp run nitro:infra:deploy -c measurement=<PCR0>` で渡し、デバッグモードなしで起動したエンクレーブから `kmstool_enclave_cli decrypt` が通ること、親で `aws kms decrypt` が AccessDenied になること、CloudTrail の `additionalEventData.recipient` を確かめる。
resume.en: Follow the user guide's "Connect the parent instance with an enclave by using virtio-vsock" and "Connect an enclave with AWS KMS" as written. Pass the PCR0 printed by `nitro-cli build-enclave` with `vp run nitro:infra:deploy -c measurement=<PCR0>`, then check that `kmstool_enclave_cli decrypt` succeeds from an enclave started without debug mode, that `aws kms decrypt` on the parent is denied, and what CloudTrail records under `additionalEventData.recipient`.

summary.ja: `lsblk --json --nodeps --output NAME,SERIAL` をインスタンスで実行していない。テストの入力は util-linux 2.40.2 のソースを読んで手で書いたもので、Amazon Linux 2023 が出す実際の JSON と突き合わせていない。
summary.en: `lsblk --json --nodeps --output NAME,SERIAL` was not run on an instance. The test input was written by hand from the util-linux 2.40.2 source and was not compared with what Amazon Linux 2023 prints.

resume.ja: 23章のインスタンスで `lsblk --json --nodeps --output NAME,SERIAL` を実行し、出力を `findDevice` に渡して、`vp run ec2:status` が示すボリューム ID のデバイスが返ることを確かめる。
resume.en: On the chapter 23 instance run `lsblk --json --nodeps --output NAME,SERIAL`, pass the output to `findDevice`, and check that it returns the device of the volume ID that `vp run ec2:status` shows.
